review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Florida Straits tagging and ICCAT synthesis support broad pelagic temperature and movement context; slope, gradient and Gulf Stream-distance response functions remain uncalibrated.

image.plan: web/fish/wahoo.png is a transparent placeholder illustration. To use a real photo: replace that file with a transparent PNG of the same name (cropped tight to the fish, facing left looks best), then set kind to "photo" and fill in credit and license here. Only use images you have the right to show: NOAA Fisheries species pages and Wikimedia Commons are good places to look; FWC illustrations are copyrighted.

profile.size: Relatively common at 50-75 lb and can exceed 100 lb
profile.diet: Almost totally fish: mackerels, butterfishes, scads, jacks, flying fish; a little squid
profile.swimming_depth: Mostly in the upper mixed layer. Tagging off Baja California found an average depth of about 18 m, with 99% of daytime above the thermocline.
profile.behavior: Solitary or in very small loose groups. More common near banks (lumps), drop-offs or weed lines in blue water, along current edges and temperature breaks. Not warm-blooded.

factors.value_notes: Wahoo sources describe pelagic association with banks, drop-offs, current lines and floating structure. These habitat associations do not validate the pipeline's 2 km bathymetric bottom_slope magnitude or a monotonic higher-is-better response; small ledges may also be smoothed out by the grid.
factors.reason_template: The seafloor drops steeply here ({value} m of depth change per km), one of the sharper ledges in the area.

factors.value_notes: Florida Straits pop-up satellite tags on four wahoo recorded more than 90% of time in approximately 17.5-27.5 °C water; ICCAT summarizes a broader 20-30 °C preferred-temperature range. This supports broad thermal context for the configured 21-30 °C band and 23-28 °C ideal, but the Florida tag sample was only four fish and does not establish a South Florida catch-probability curve.
factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside the {ideal_min}-{ideal_max} C range where wahoo are most active.

factors.value_notes: Angler sources describe fishing temperature breaks and current edges, but reviewed biological sources do not quantify wahoo response to the runtime scalar SST-gradient magnitude. Relative ranking against the day's sharpest breaks is not a validated species suitability curve.
factors.reason_template: Water temperature changes about {per10km} C every 10 km here, one of the sharper breaks in the area today.

factors.value_notes: The existing source is angler guidance about water-color edges. No reviewed species-specific study validates remotely sensed chlorophyll-gradient magnitude as a monotonic wahoo suitability factor; retain provisional status.
factors.reason_template: A strong water color edge is present, where wahoo patrol for bait.

factors.value_notes: ICCAT describes wahoo association with current lines, floating objects and oceanic features, supporting a broad current-feature association. The sources do not directly validate the runtime current_convergence calculation or its higher-is-better response.
factors.reason_template: Converging currents aggregate weed lines and bait along drop-offs.

factors.value_notes: The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetric depth. Florida Straits tagging describes fish vertical occupancy (more than 90% of time above 200 m), and ICCAT describes epipelagic use in the upper mixed layer; neither establishes preferred seabed depth. Retain only as a weak offshore/nearshore screen; configured numeric intervals remain unvalidated.
factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in the blue water wahoo use.

factors.value_notes: ICCAT reports year-round presence in the Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico and summer spawning in the northwest Atlantic (June-August, including Florida and the Bahamas); the Florida Museum reports western-central Atlantic spawning mainly May-August. These sources do not validate the configured October-March angler-derived fishing window or November-February peak months as a South Florida catch curve.

value_text.peak: It is prime wahoo season (about November to February) off South Florida.
value_text.in_season: It is wahoo season off South Florida (about October to March).
value_text.off: It is outside the usual wahoo peak, though wahoo are caught year-round.

factors.value_notes: ICCAT summarizes extensive East Florida wahoo movements that may be associated with the Gulf Stream. This supports regional movement context, not a preferred distance-response relationship; the configured -35 to 40 km range and -6 to 15 km ideal remain unvalidated.
factors.reason_template: The Gulf Stream's inshore edge is close ({abs_value} km {side}). Wahoo patrol current edges.

timing.note: Angler lore: patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies. Numbers are judgment calls to be calibrated against trip logs.

text.dawn: It is dawn, the low-light time when wahoo are reported to bite best.
text.dusk: It is dusk, the low-light time when wahoo are reported to bite best.

moon.text: It is the week around the full moon, when local charters report the year's best wahoo fishing with the king tides.
